title: factdiff resolve and review_items call Doc.locate with cites=1, so a data row anchored with several citations may not relocate
goal: Every caller of Doc.locate (factdiff.py resolve and review_items, census.py) passes the fact's real citation count, as anchoring does, so a data row located by the second look relocates on a changed page as modified instead of falling to not-found or score.

run: import re,sys; f=open("_tools/factdiff.py").read(); c=open("_tools/census.py").read(); bad=re.findall(r"\.locate\(fact_text\([^()]*\)\)",f)+re.findall(r"\.locate\(claim\)",c); sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)

repro_reason: the cited-data-row case needs a changed live page; the repro reads every Doc.locate call that passes no citation count (factdiff.py, census.py), and the added test selection runs the relocation
notes: Planned at the 2026-10-12 draft triage (sprint 6 of 19, "Freshness at lookup: revalidation compares the right window and remembers what it checked"): it serves the fitness tests of EP-gzr4mmkm: a lookup's verdict or the benchmark's measurement is wrong until it is fixed. Premise: Doc.locate is called without the citation count outside anchoring. Run 2026-10-12 on origin/main: the repro finds 7 such calls (factdiff.py elsewhere, resolve, new_passage, old_passage, review_items; census.py current_passage, repin_item), so the repro fails now. Anchoring takes the count from one Counter over every source cited_facts; resolve and review_items hold one source facts, so that Counter is passed in. The test name carries resolve_relocates_multi_citation_row (test_live_kb.py; census callers in test_redact.py). Run after ST-gtaw5kip: both change factdiff.py resolve.
